notes: TASK #81 ADDITION. content/raws/barks/contract_barks.json is UNTOUCHED. Two things this file does. FIRST, it wires the register (see content/raws/barks/tone_barks.json's own notes on DialogueDirector::toned()) into the moment a radiant offer actually reaches the player: being handed a job, being paid for one, being turned away, and being told there is simply nothing tonight. SECOND, some of these keys are the only place a line for a given key exists at all -- contract.none.polite / contract.none.blunt / contract.blocked.polite / contract.blocked.blunt are GENERIC (no per-broker table sits ahead of them in any broker's resolve chain, so they reach every broker who hits that state), while contract.take.<id>.polite/.blunt and contract.paid.<id>.polite/.blunt are PER-BROKER on purpose -- contract_barks.json already gives cull, venn and finch their own untagged contract.take/contract.paid table, and DialogueDirector::toned() widens a chain broker-specific-then-generic, so a generic contract.take.polite table would sit BEHIND cull's own untagged contract.take.cull in every resolve and would be dead content, exactly the bug this task found and fixed in contract.none. contract.paid.polite/.blunt stays generic in addition to cull's and finch's own tables because venn has no contract.paid.venn table of his own to shadow it -- the generic pair is what colours HIS payout.

rows: Manners, in the impound yard. That's a first one. Take it, and mind the number the same as I'd have told you either way.
Please, is it. Fine. The rats don't care how nicely you ask for them, but go on. Bring the scalps to me, not the yard.
You could have just said take it. But go on, be that sort. Bring a priest's word with them when you're done.
Good. No wasted breath. Take it -- the number's the number, same as always.
That is the whole conversation I want out of anybody standing in this yard. Go.
Straight to it. I like a man who does not make me listen to him first.
Ask nicely and I still might not answer you. But it is a better start than most give me. Down the stair, past the snug.
Polite goes further in my cellar than it does at the Weighhouse. Do not stop to drink it on the way down.
There. See how much easier that was than making me guess what you wanted.
Fine, no wasted words. Down the stair, past the snug, and do not drink it.
Good. I have no patience for a long ask over a short job.
That is how I like my custom -- quick in, quick out, quick paid.
Careful with me. Politeness is a thing people remember, and remembering is the one thing this work cannot afford.
Ask however you like. What you carry back had better speak plainer than you do.
Fine words do not count for anything up here. The count does. Go.
Good. Say less, and none of it out loud.
That is the roofs' own manners -- none. Go.
Short and quiet. Keep both the whole way there.
Manners AND the scalps counted right. I could get used to that, and I will not let myself.
Counted, marked and paid -- and thank you kindly, noted, though the ward's coin says it whether you are civil or not.
Counted. Paid. Go.
That is the coin. No speech needed on either end of this counter.
Polite AND quick. That combination gets rarer every year I do this.
Counted. And I will remember the manners longer than I will remember the coin.
Counted. Gone.
Good count, fewer words. That is the whole of this trade.
Counted properly, and asked for properly. Small mercies, in this ward.
There is your coin, and my thanks for not making this longer than it needed to be.
Counted. Paid. Done.
No speeches. Here is your coin.
Ask as nicely as you like -- I still do not know you well enough to hand you anything.
Kind of you to ask so properly. The answer is still no.
No. Come back when I know you.
Nothing for you. Do not make me say it twice.
Nothing tonight, and thank you for asking rather than just standing there waiting on it.
Kindly asked, honestly answered: there is nothing for you right now.
Nothing. Come back later.
Empty tonight. Do not ask twice.
